summary: The pain is real, but the evidence comes from in-house admins on old Q&A threads and from an enterprise survey, not from small MSSPs saying they would pay. Many targets run Wazuh or Graylog Open or flat-priced SIEMs with no ingest bill, and free maintained configs exist. The serviceable market is likely low thousands of firms at $3k/year. Demand is unproven until pilots convert.

objections.objection: The people complaining are not the named buyer. The need statements come from in-house sysadmins asking ServerFault or Security.SE how to log terminal-server logons or quiet Graylog. None comes from an MSSP owner who pays a recurring fee to fix Windows volume. Q&A questions show a how-to gap, not purchase intent, and they are mostly answered with free GPO and audit-policy advice.

The evidence is old. The top need statement ('Terminal Server Logging', 114 engagement) was asked in May 2009. The SIEM pre-filtering question dates from Aug 2013, 'SIEM system, what are the benefits?' from Dec 2011, 'OSSEC as a SIEM' from Sep 2013 and the Graylog audit-noise post from Sep 2021. No recent signal shows small MSSPs asking for this, so the concept cannot show that the pain is urgent now.

The cost-pain evidence describes the wrong segment. The Help Net Security/Dynatrace report surveyed 450 senior IT leaders at large enterprises, with about $2.5M a year spent on logging. It says nothing about a 5-analyst MSSP. Several SIEMs the concept names have no per-GB bill: Wazuh and Graylog Open are self-hosted, and Blumira and Huntress are flat-priced. Those MSSPs pay in disk and hardware, not licences, so a $249/month dollar-savings pitch is weak for them. The concept admits this share is unknown.

Free alternatives already cover the core need. sysmon-modular is actively maintained, builds versioned configs for several Sysmon releases, has an MDE-augment profile and has ATT&CK-mapped modules. It is close to what the paid tier promises. Buyers who already use free community content are not a budgeted market. Microsoft's built-in Sysmon also takes custom configs, so the value left to sell is narrow: per-SIEM mappings plus a volume report.

The market is small. Security-led MSPs and MSSPs with 2-15 analysts that pay volume-billed SIEM ingest for Windows-heavy SMB fleets probably number in the low thousands worldwide. At $249/month (about $3k/year), even 150 customers is under $0.5M ARR. That can support a solo lifestyle business, not a venture-scale one, and the concept gives no count of target firms.

The logon-evidence and ransomware-precursor packs widen the pitch, but their own demand evidence is equally anecdotal. Those buyers already have budgeted products: ADAudit Plus from $245-$595/year, EDR bundles and backup vendors' anti-ransomware. The concept does not show these packs would win budget from tools MSPs already resell.

strongest_point: The riskiest-assumption test is cheap, fast and well designed: a free baseline, a log-diet script and $500 hand-done pilots will show real willingness to pay within weeks.
what_would_change_my_mind: 3 or more paid $500 pilots and 10 or more MSSPs asking for subscription pricing within two weeks of the r/msp and Wazuh/Graylog posts
Interviews with 15 small MSSPs in which at least half pay per-GB SIEM ingest and name Windows events as their biggest line
Recent (2025-2026) posts from MSSP owners complaining about Windows ingest cost
A measured Windows-volume cut of 40% or more in the pilots, worth more than $249/month per MSSP
